summary:
G3 English review of EFMP-302 Unit 4 at commit 482eb52 (bound Unit 4 inputs identical to 820003d). Disposition: escalate. Five of seven criteria pass; sources and accessibility fail, both on the same artifact.

Run 006's single blocking finding IS repaired. RRQ-05 now asks something the unit teaches, its mark scheme sums to 5 and no longer contradicts itself, it duplicates neither RRQ-06 nor RRQ-07, and fig-U4-3 now agrees with topic-02's prose on where indicators sit. All 25 assessment items were solved independently before the key was read; all 10 MCQ keys agree and all 10 RRQ schemes sum. The check:no-answer-keys exclusion is now correctly scoped to specs/content/<course>/reviews and both regression tests pass. assessment therefore passes.

What blocks. Commit 0222168 rewrote fig-U4-3's caption without re-checking it, and the new line collides with the site wordmark by 4.5 px in an identical vertical band, in both theme variants; at the parent commit the same line cleared the wordmark by 11.2 px, so this is a regression introduced by the repair. The same new caption asserts that "Most" indicators come from the performance band - a quantitative claim about a primary document nobody in this pipeline has read, absent from every topic file, and not among the three claims the unverifiable-sources declaration discloses as uncorroborated.

Why escalate rather than revise. Both defects are precisely located and cheaply repairable, so a revise would be defensible on content alone. But this is the seventh G3 cycle against a stated limit of two, and it is the fifth in which a repair closed its target and introduced or left a defect in the same artifact. Authorising an eighth cycle is an owner decision. Fourteen advisories are carried forward, none of them blocking.

This report is advisory. It is not a signature, a registry entry, a qualification record, a tracker transition or an acceptance.

findings.message:
NEW at commit 0222168, the repair under review. fig-U4-3's caption overprints the site wordmark, in BOTH theme variants. `accessibility` fails on this.

static/img/figures/efmp-302/unit-04/fig-U4-3.svg and fig-U4-3.dark.svg, viewBox "0 0 880 470", carried at docs/semester-1/efmp-302/unit-04/topic-02.mdx:24.
  caption line 1  <text class="m" x="30" y="444">   measured bbox x 30.0 -> 780.1, y 433.9 -> 446.5
  wordmark        <text class="wm" x="868" y="444">  measured bbox x 775.6 -> 868.5, y 433.9 -> 446.5
The two runs overlap by 4.5 px in an identical vertical band, so the glyphs paint on top of one another and the line renders as "...because knowledge and[t]extbook.com.pk". Both are mid-greys (.m = var(--muted) #566b65 light / #9aa7a2 dark; .wm = var(--wm) #8b9a95 light / #6b7671 dark), so neither wins.

ATTRIBUTION, measured rather than assumed. At the parent commit b131081 the then caption line 1 ("Only the performance band produces indicators, ...") ended at x2 = 764.4, clear of the wordmark's x = 775.6 by 11.2 px, and the collision test returned empty. Commit 0222168 replaced that line with a longer one and did not re-check the geometry. This is therefore a regression introduced by the repair, not a carried defect.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING COSMETIC. The overprinted phrase is in the sentence that commit 0222168 exists to install - the corrected statement of where indicators sit. It is the one line of this figure a reader is most likely to be checking against topic-02's prose.

Evidence: renders-agent-g3-efmp302-u4-run007/crop-desktop-fig-U4-3-run007.png, crop-dark-fig-U4-3-run007.png; measurement in logs-agent-g3-efmp302-u4-run007/render-review.log.
REPAIR (author's choice, not the reviewer's): shorten caption line 1, rewrap it, or move the wordmark to y=462 or below the caption block. Whichever is chosen, fig-U4-3.dark.svg must change identically and figures:variants:check must be re-run.
NOTE FOR THE GATE OWNER: check:figures exits 0 and cannot see this. No gate in the set measures text geometry inside a committed SVG.

NEW at commit 0222168. fig-U4-3's replacement caption asserts a quantitative claim about the primary document that no one in this pipeline has read, and the unverifiable-sources declaration does not disclose it. `sources` fails on this.

The caption now reads, in both variants:
  "Indicators sit beneath the parts, and only indicators produce evidence. Most come from the
   performance band, because knowledge and dispositions are inferred from what performance
   shows, which is why a standard can be met in appearance while understanding is absent."

Three separate things there. The first clause now agrees with docs/semester-1/efmp-302/unit-04/topic-02.mdx:64-66 ("Beneath the parts sit indicators") and with topic-02's Summary - that half of the run-006 finding IS repaired. The problem is "Most come from the performance band".

1. IT IS A FREQUENCY CLAIM ABOUT THE NPST'S ACTUAL INDICATORS. specs/content/efmp-302/coverage/unit-04.md grounds U4-05 (topic-02 "### The structure of Pakistan's National Professional Standards for Teachers", which is the section fig-U4-3 illustrates) in npst-pakistan-2009. That key is declared unretrievable at specs/content/efmp-302/sources/unit-04.md:40 and nobody has read its indicators.
2. THE DECLARATION DOES NOT COVER IT. The declaration states exactly what the unread source leaves uncorroborated: "the ten standard names, the three-part division and the 2009 MoE/UNESCO/USAID origin". The distribution of indicators across the three parts is a fourth claim and is not listed. The G3 reference is explicit that a declaration which understates what it leaves unchecked remains a failure, and that prose stating more than the declaration supports still fails `sources`.
3. IT IS TAUGHT NOWHERE ELSE. No topic file makes this claim. The nearest passage, topic-02.mdx "Try this at your practicum school" ("Most trainees discover that the dispositions part is nearly impossible to evidence by watching"), is about what an observer can see in one lesson, framed as a practicum discovery - not about how the document distributes its indicators. The claim exists only inside the SVG.

RELATION TO THE PRIOR RECORD. The second clause, "knowledge and dispositions are inferred from what performance shows", is CARRIED: it was present pre-repair at b131081 and no run flagged it as unsourced. What is new is the softened frequency quantifier "Most come from", which replaced the absolute "Only the performance band produces indicators" that run 006 rejected on internal-contradiction grounds. The repair fixed the contradiction with the prose and left the unverified empirical claim standing in weaker form. This is the same defect class - an unsourced frequency generalisation - that runs 001 to 004 repaired three times on Isore.

Also note the band sub-label inside the same figure: "what the teacher can do: the part that can be seen, and therefore the part that is assessed". That asserts of the NPST that only the performance part is assessed, which sits awkwardly beside topic-02's own argument that the three-part division exists precisely because knowing, valuing and doing are separately diagnosable.

REPAIR OPTIONS, for the author and owner to choose between: (a) restate the caption as the epistemic point the unit actually teaches, e.g. that indicators are easiest to write for the performance band because that is what an observer can see, with no claim about how many the document has; or (b) add the indicator-distribution claim to the `## Unverifiable sources` disclosure for npst-pakistan-2009 so the declaration stops understating what is unchecked; or (c) obtain the primary document and check it.

CARRIED AND STILL OPEN, from run-005 [11] through run-006 [1]. PROCESS, not content. This is why the run escalates rather than returning a bare `revise`.

It interacts with the two blocking findings above in a way the owner should see plainly. Run 006's blocking finding IS resolved. In closing it, commit 0222168 introduced one new rendering regression and left one unverified claim standing in the same artifact. Runs 002, 003, 004 and 006 each recorded the same shape: a repair that closes the named defect and displaces or introduces another in the same file. An eighth automatic cycle is unlikely to break that pattern; authorising one is an owner decision, not a reviewer's.

Verified in the rendered DOM, not only in source: the alt measured 223 characters at desktop:topic-02.
  CONCEPT-GRAPH PREMISE, checked rather than taken on trust: specs/content/efmp-302/concepts/unit-04.md maps CON:EFMP-302-4-7 to MCQ-04 and RRQ-05, and CON:EFMP-302-4-9 to RRQ-05 and ERQ-02. RRQ-05 is indeed the only RRQ assessing either, so keeping the architecture clause was necessary.

VERDICT ON RUN-006 [10] - the breadth of the check:no-answer-keys review exclusion. RESOLVED, and adequately.

scripts/check-no-answer-keys.mjs:57 now defines REVIEW_EVIDENCE_DIR = /^specs[/\\]content[/\\][^/\\]+[/\\]reviews$/ and line 139 applies it: `if (name === 'reviews' && REVIEW_EVIDENCE_DIR.test(relative(ROOT, p))) continue;`. The skip is now exactly `specs/content/<course>/reviews` - one path segment for the course, anchored at both ends - rather than any directory named `reviews` anywhere under TARGETS. A `docs/**/reviews/` or `licence/**/reviews/` directory is scanned again, which was the latent risk.

Two regression tests exist and both were executed this run, not merely read: tests/unit/no-answer-keys.test.mjs:119 "skips specs/content/<course>/reviews/, which holds unpublished review evidence" and :128 "still scans a reviews/ directory under a published content root". `npx vitest run tests/unit/no-answer-keys.test.mjs` exits 0, 10/10 passing (logs-agent-g3-efmp302-u4-run007/no-answer-keys-regression-tests.log). The second test is the one that matters, because it pins the behaviour the narrowing was for.

`npm run check:no-answer-keys` exits 0 at this commit. Adequate; no residual.

CARRIED AND STILL OPEN from run-006 [11], and it generalises beyond the items run 006 measured. Re-derived independently this run across the whole RRQ band.

Of the 59 marks in the ten RRQ schemes, roughly 43 pay for naming, listing or describing taught content and roughly 16 for explanation. Explanation marks per item: RRQ-01 1/4, RRQ-02 0/7, RRQ-03 1/8, RRQ-04 4/4, RRQ-05 1/5, RRQ-06 2/4, RRQ-07 2/5, RRQ-08 2/9, RRQ-09 0/9 (wholly descriptive), RRQ-10 4/4.

So the pattern run 006 found in RRQ-03 is the band's norm rather than an artefact of the rewrites. Seven of ten items carry an *(Understand)* label, and three carry *(Analyze)*; the three Analyze items (04, 07, 10) are also the three whose marks are mostly or wholly explanation, so the labels are honest. But an item such as RRQ-05, rewritten precisely to add a non-recall clause, still pays 4 of 5 marks for recitation. A candidate can score 80 per cent of RRQ-05 and 87.5 per cent of RRQ-03 without doing any of the thinking the item was rewritten to demand.

specs/content/efmp-302/content-spec.md:675-676 requires of the unit-end bank: "RRQs (10): Understand to Analyze; >= 2 per topic; each with a model answer and a point-by-point mark scheme". The section is headed "### RRQ model answers and mark schemes".

NEW this run. Two taught passages pull in opposite directions on whether one document can serve both purposes, and no passage reconciles them for the student.

docs/semester-1/efmp-302/unit-04/topic-03.mdx states, in bold and as an imperative: "**Self-evaluation and appraisal must not be the same document.**"
docs/semester-1/efmp-302/unit-04/topic-04.mdx teaches the opposite emphasis from Isore: the purposes are "often conflicting" but "**but not necessarily incompatible**", a single framework "can serve both summative and formative purposes", and "It is not a proof that one document can never do both."
The two are reconcilable - topic-03 is about a developmental record feeding a consequential decision, topic-04 about a framework serving two purposes by design - but nothing in the unit says so.
It becomes assessable rather than merely stylistic at RRQ-04's mark scheme, unit-assessment.mdx:222-226: "Do not award an answer whose conclusion is that one document cannot hold both". A candidate who took topic-03's bolded imperative at face value is penalised by an instruction the unit never warned them about. RRQ-04's stem does presuppose that one document can serve both and asks what must be decided, so the instruction is defensible as written; the gap is in the teaching, not the marking. One sentence in topic-04 distinguishing "one framework, two purposes" from "one document, two uses" would close it.

specs/content/efmp-302/content-spec.md "## Unit 4" introduces the sub-topic checklist as "One row per leaf bullet of course-guide sections 4.1-4.4". Read against the bound guide, that is not literally what it is.
